A 15 July 2025 official Polynesie francaise Ministry of Health / ARASS note, published on service-public.pf under the DGAE path, was downloaded and visually rendered. Page 1 visibly identifies Polynesie francaise and the Ministry of Health / ARASS, states the object as products of cannabis authorized in French Polynesia and their import conditions / professional obligations, and cites Loi du pays n 2024-19 of 23 August 2024 and Arrete n 118 CM of 6 February 2025 regulating activities relating to cannabis without narcotic properties and medicines containing cannabis or cannabinoids. rows.differenceDescription: The official Journal Officiel de la Republique Gabonaise Code penal page was opened live with HTTP 200 and visually captured. Article 208 visibly names cannabis and its derivatives among plants or poisonous substances classified as narcotics, along with opium, heroin, morphine, cocaine, kat, LSD and psychotropics, and punishes illicit use with imprisonment up to one year and a fine up to 1,500,000 francs. The same article includes a medical-treatment clause for an illicit user, allowing the court to order medical supervision or detox and potentially not pronounce the use penalty, but the reviewed source does not establish a regulated medical cannabis program. The trafficking title and Articles 408-410 were visually captured: Article 408 punishes organizing transport, possession, offering, transfer, distribution, commercialization, acquisition or illicit use of narcotics with thirty years reclusion and a fine equal to five times the seizure value; Article 409 punishes illicit production or fabrication with twenty years reclusion and up to 50,000,000 francs; Article 410 punishes illicit import/export with twenty years reclusion and a fine equal to five times the seizure value, with organized-band penalties up to thirty years and very high fines. Article 413 visibly states narcotics are substances or plants classified as such by law or regulation. Project recreational=ILLEGAL, medical=NONE and enforcement=STRICT are supported by this reviewed official evidence. No project status SSOT was changed.

directOfficialCannabisLawLinks.note: Grenada is visually verified from official Grenada Parliament PDFs. Act No. 1 of 2026 is a real law/scope change against the project row: it creates decriminalised personal cannabis quantities of 56g cannabis / 15g resin, recognises medical/therapeutic/scientific cannabis routes, treats four or fewer plants differently, adds Rastafarian religious-use authorization mechanisms, and softens some minor/public-use enforcement while retaining strict controlled-drug penalties outside those exceptions. Project ILLEGAL/NONE/STRICT is therefore outdated/too coarse.

rows.differenceDescription: Micronesia is visually verified from the official FSM Law / FSM Code Title 11 Chapter 11 Controlled Substances law text. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and medical=NONE are supported, with medical caveat that the reviewed law contains only a general controlled-substance practitioner/registration authorization and no cannabis-specific patient program. Project enforcement=STRICT is broadly supported for trafficking, unauthorized supply and larger possession, but the row needs an explicit caveat because one ounce or less of marihuana is fine-only and first-offense possession may receive conditional discharge. No project status SSOT was changed.
